Bug_Details:
A field was set twice in the same chained expression. Proto and AutoValue builders provide a fluent interface for constructing
instances. Unlike argument lists, however, they do not prevent the user from
providing multiple values for the same field. Setting the same field multiple times in the same chained expression is
pointless (as the intermediate value will be overwritten), and can easily mask a
bug, especially if the setter is called with different arguments. return MyProto.newBuilder()
    .setFoo(copy.getFoo())
    .setFoo(copy.getBar())
    .build(); return MyProto.newBuilder()
    .setFoo(copy.getFoo())
    .setFoo(copy.getBar())
    .build();
Bug_Explanation: The bug is that the `setFoo` method is called twice on the same object in the same chained expression, which is redundant. The first call to `setFoo` sets the value of `foo` to the value of `bar`, then the second call overrides that value with `foo`. This is pointless and can easily mask a bug, especially if the setter is called with different arguments.
